data.turoyo: Mor Malke naḥət kile kboxən w kəmwalwəli w ksaymi w rayəḥ w ǧeye, walḥasəl maqəmme i qyəmto
data.translation: Mor Malke ging hin (zu ihnen), sie weinten und jammerten, machten dies und jenes, kurz und gut, sie machten einen richtigen Aufstand.

rationale: Third Infectum example; plural lamenters and an independently understandable public-distress context.

data.turoyo: Azzano, kəlla i qiyəmto qayimo, ʕamo kule aṯi, kboxe, mwalwəl.
data.translation: We went; look, there was a great uproar, all the people had come, weeping and wailing.

rationale: Infectum has three examples after round 1; add one concise collective-subject lament, with mwalwəl beside kboxe. Supplied machine English, cut before the subsequent hospital/quotation narrative.

summary: All three occurrences checked. 24/281 and 29/122 are already quoted and are not duplicated. The inherited stem label I is retained despite the four-consonant root.
The Arabic expressive loan behaves as a finite verb: third-singular masculine, third-singular feminine and plural mwalwəli. It is not a light-verb-plus-noun construction.

Lamentation accompanies both grief with breast beating and quiet fear. Manner and stimulus differences stay within jammern, without new senses. In JTM, plural -i contrasts with neighbouring kboxən; do not infer a new stem from the different agreement shape.
The single new occurrence agrees with inherited I mwalwele/mwalwəl and sense 1 jammern. Keep the editorial I designation despite the four-consonant root; no new Q stem is proposed.

ʕAmo kule is a collective subject with singular-looking mwalwəl, contrasted with round 1 plural mwalwəli. Co-occurring kboxe supplies simultaneous crying; grief is contextual, not a separately numbered sense.
The Infectum cell rises from three after round 1 to four. No new idiom, causative or Detransitive is established. English is the unchanged project machine translation.
Does printed gmalwəlo at 29/122 reflect reduction of mwalwəl, or transcription variation relative to the inherited g-mwalwəlo? Preserve both supplied spellings pending source verification.
Jan 1.21/1045: confirm whether singular mwalwəl with collective ʕamo is ordinary agreement; no new form or stem is inferred from it.
